d1: close view of the lower part of a freshly limewashed chalky white exterior wall, a strong jet of water from a green garden hose nozzle hitting the white paint at chest height, water sheeting down the wall
d2: the same wall wet and shiny, water running down in streams, the chalky white paint still intact, the jet still hitting

A: the neighbor stands behind the low unplastered brick wall on the right with his arms crossed, shaking his head, talking to the presenter
K: the neighbor behind the low brick wall with arms crossed, head tilted, sceptical half smile, the presenter beside the white wall holding the hose pointed down
line: ¿Con cal y cemento? Con la primera lluvia se te lava todo, te lo digo yo.
text: ¿Con cal y cemento? Con la primera lluvia se te lava todo, te lo digo yo.

A: he lifts the hose pistol and sprays the white half of the wall again at close range, water splashing, glancing at the neighbor
K: he holds the green hose pistol spraying the white half of the wall, water running down, he looks sideways at the neighbor with a small calm smile
text: Mira.

A: he lowers the hose, turns to the camera and talks, pointing back at the wet white wall with his thumb
K: he faces the camera holding the dripping hose down at his side, thumb pointing back over his shoulder at the wet white wall, eyebrows raised
text: Loco o genio: pinté la casa con cemento, cal y agua. Y no se cae.

d1: close view of a plastic jug pouring white hydrated lime powder into an empty grey plastic twenty-litre bucket on a concrete floor, a puff of white dust rising
d2: the same bucket with a heap of white lime powder inside, a little dust still floating above it
text: Cal hidratada.

A: he tips a plastic jug of fine white cement powder into the bucket on the workbench, looking at the camera
K: he holds the empty plastic jug above the bucket, a thin trail of white powder still falling, looking at the camera
text: Cemento blanco, poquito.

d1: close view of a plastic jug pouring clear water into a grey bucket of white powder, the water turning milky
d2: the same bucket now full of milky white liquid with small ripples on the surface
text: Agua.

A: he holds up a small glass jar of coarse salt next to the bucket and shakes it toward the camera with a half smile
K: he holds the glass jar of coarse grey salt at face height beside his cheek, one eyebrow raised, looking at the camera
text: Y un cuarto ingrediente, que casi nadie pone.

d1: close view of a wooden stick stirring thick milky white limewash in a grey bucket, swirls on the surface
d2: the same bucket with a smooth creamy white surface, the stick lifted, white liquid dripping from it
text: Se revuelve hasta que queda como leche.

A: he dips a wide white-bristle brush into a bucket of limewash and paints a long stroke on the old grey wall, talking
K: a long fresh stroke of pale translucent white on the grey old wall, the wet brush resting against the wall, he looks at the camera
text: Y con una brocha ancha, sobre el repello, manos finitas.

d1: close view of a wide brush laying limewash on bare grey cement plaster, the paint looking thin and see-through as it goes on
d2: the same patch of wall covered with an even thin milky coat, the brush lifting away at the edge of the frame
text: La primera mano parece que no tapa nada.

A: he walks slowly along the wall and stops at the line where the chalky white half meets the old grey stained half, touching both
K: he stands at the dividing line, his right palm on the bright white half and his left palm on the old grey stained half, looking at the camera
text: Pero mira el antes y el después, en la misma pared.

A: he rubs his palm hard on the white half and shows the camera his clean palm
K: he holds his open right palm toward the camera, the palm clean with no white dust, the white wall behind him
text: Froto, y no me deja la mano blanca.

A: he gestures to the whole wall with an open arm while talking to the camera, calm and sure
K: he stands in front of the wall with his left arm open toward the white half, looking at the camera with a confident small nod
text: Y va aguada, así que rinde muchísimo. Con un balde pinto toda esta pared, y me sobra.

A: he knocks on the white wall with his knuckles and explains to the camera
K: his knuckles resting on the white wall, he looks at the camera explaining, serious
text: ¿Por qué no se cae? Porque no es una capa de plástico pegada encima. La cal se mete en los poros del repello.

A: he runs his fingertips along the texture of the white wall, then looks at the camera
K: his fingertips on the white chalky surface, he looks at the camera with a small smile
text: Y con el aire, poco a poco, se vuelve piedra otra vez. Por eso no se descascara como la pintura común.

A: he glances at the neighbor behind the low wall and back to the camera, amused
K: he looks at the camera with an amused face, his thumb pointing sideways toward the neighbor behind the low brick wall
text: Mi vecino todavía no me cree. Ya le voy a mostrar.

A: he raises a finger and leans toward the camera, lowering his voice a little
K: he leans slightly toward the camera with his index finger raised, eyebrows up, conspiratorial face
text: Pero ojo: el cuarto ingrediente es el que hace que no se caiga, y casi nadie lo pone bien. Al final te enseño el error.

A: he puts the salt jar down on the workbench and spreads his hands over the bucket, talking to the camera
K: he stands behind the workbench, hands resting on both sides of the grey bucket, looking at the camera
text: Te doy la receta completa ya, con las medidas, y después te muestro cada paso de cerca.

A: he holds up an empty plastic one-litre jug and taps it
K: he holds the empty clear plastic jug up at shoulder height, tapping its side with a finger, looking at the camera
text: Todo se mide con el mismo recipiente. Yo uso esta jarra. No en kilos: en jarras.

A: he scoops lime powder with the jug from the open paper bag four times into the bucket, counting on his fingers
K: he holds four fingers up with his left hand, the jug in his right hand dusty with white powder, looking at the camera
text: Cuatro jarras de cal hidratada.

A: he scoops one jug of white cement from a smaller bag and shows one finger
K: he holds one finger up, the jug in the other hand dusted white, the small bag of white cement open on the bench
text: Una jarra de cemento blanco. Cuatro a uno.

A: he tips a handful of coarse salt from the jar into a mug of steaming hot water and stirs it with a spoon
K: he stirs the mug with a spoon, steam rising, looking at the camera
text: Un puñado de sal gruesa, disuelta antes en un poco de agua caliente.

A: he pours water from a large plastic jug into the bucket while stirring with a wooden stick
K: he stirs the bucket with the wooden stick, milky white liquid inside, looking down at it
text: Y agua, más o menos el doble que de polvo, hasta que quede como leche. Leche, no yogur.

A: he taps the side of the bucket and raises a warning finger
K: he holds his index finger up beside the bucket, serious look at the camera
text: Y la pared tiene que ser mineral: repello, ladrillo o cemento. Sobre pintura plástica, no. Ya te explico por qué.

A: he taps the bucket lid and points at a calendar hanging on the wall, talking
K: he rests a hand on the bucket lid, pointing with the other hand toward the wall of the garage, looking at the camera
text: La cal la dejo remojando desde la noche anterior. El cemento y la sal van el día que pinto.

d1: close view of milky limewash being poured from a bucket through a piece of green mosquito mesh stretched over another bucket
d2: the second bucket full of smooth white limewash, the mesh holding a few small lumps
text: Se cuela, para que no queden grumos.

A: he sprays the old grey wall with a garden pump sprayer, the plaster darkening where it gets wet
K: the wall is darker grey and damp where he sprayed, he holds the pump sprayer lowered, looking at the camera
text: La pared limpia, sin pintura plástica, y mojada antes de pintar.

A: he paints another thin stroke with the wide brush, then holds up three fingers
K: he holds up three fingers of his left hand, the brush in his right hand, a few thin white strokes on the grey wall behind him
text: Tres o cuatro manos finas, dejando secar entre una y otra.

A: he mists the painted wall lightly with the pump sprayer and nods to the camera
K: a fine mist settles on the painted wall, he lowers the sprayer and nods at the camera
text: Y los días siguientes, un rocío de agua para que cure despacio. Eso es todo.

A: he puts the sprayer down and talks to the camera, counting the questions on his fingers
K: he holds up two fingers, looking at the camera with a friendly serious face
text: Ahora sí, vamos con las preguntas que más me hicieron, porque ahí es donde la gente la arruina.

A: he lifts the lid of an old bucket with hardened grey-white lumps inside and shows it to the camera
K: he holds the lid up with one hand, the old bucket with hard lumpy white paste inside tilted toward the camera, disgusted face
text: La primera, y la que más se repite: ¿se puede guardar para el otro día? Mira lo que pasa.

d1: close view of a stick pushing into a thick lumpy grey-white paste in a bucket, the paste cracking in chunks
d2: the stick stuck upright in the hardened lumpy paste
text: Esto lo preparé ayer con el cemento adentro. Grumos. Ya no pinta igual, por más que lo revuelvas.

A: he taps the bag of white cement with his finger, explaining
K: his finger rests on the paper bag of white cement on the bench, he looks at the camera explaining
text: ¿Por qué? Porque el cemento empieza a fraguar en cuanto le cae agua. No espera a que tú termines.

A: he puts the lid back on the old bucket and slides it away across the bench
K: the old bucket is pushed to the far end of the bench, lid on, he looks at the camera with a small shrug
text: Entonces la regla es sencilla: el cemento se mezcla sólo con lo que vas a usar ese día.

A: he pats the lid of another bucket full of soaked lime paste, satisfied
K: his palm flat on the lid of the lime paste bucket, satisfied smile at the camera
text: La cal sola, en cambio, sí aguanta. Tapada, con un dedito de agua encima, dura semanas. Por eso separo.

A: he holds up a clear plastic jug of lime powder next to a kitchen scale, comparing
K: he holds the jug of white powder above a small kitchen scale on the bench, looking at the camera with raised eyebrows
text: Segunda pregunta: ¿kilos o botes? Un bote de cal no pesa lo mismo que un bote de cemento.

A: he puts the jug on the scale, reads it, then puts a same jug of cement on the scale
K: the jug of cement sits on the small scale, he points at it looking at the camera
text: La cal es mucho más liviana. Si mides la cal en kilos y el cemento en jarras, te sale otra mezcla.

A: he taps the same jug twice, nodding
K: he holds the clear jug up next to his face, nodding at the camera
text: Por eso todo en jarras, con la misma jarra. Cuatro de cal, una de cemento. Así no te equivocas nunca.

A: he sits on a stool by the bench and holds up four fingers, thinking
K: he sits on the stool with four fingers raised, a thoughtful look at the camera
text: Cuarta pregunta: ¿cuánto dura? No te voy a inventar un número. Depende de la lluvia, del sol, y de cómo la pongas.

A: he stands up from the stool and pats the bucket of lime, smiling
K: he stands with one hand on the lime bucket, a warm smile at the camera
text: Lo bueno es que cuando se gasta no hay que raspar nada: se moja y se le pasa otra mano encima, y queda como nueva.

A: he stands in a small bedroom next to a wall painted with old glossy cream latex paint and knocks on it
K: he stands beside the old cream latex wall, his knuckles against it, looking at the camera
text: Y la tercera: ¿la puedo poner encima de la pintura que ya tengo? Aquí está la parte honesta.

A: he presses a strip of masking tape on a small test patch of dried limewash on the latex wall and pulls it off
K: he holds up the strip of tape toward the camera, the tape covered in white flakes, a bare patch visible on the wall
text: Sobre látex, esmalte o pintura plástica, se agarra mal. Mira la cinta: se llevó todo.

A: he points at the test patch on the latex wall, serious
K: he points at the flaking test patch on the cream latex wall, serious face at the camera
text: La cal necesita un fondo mineral para meterse: repello, ladrillo, cemento. El plástico no la deja entrar.

A: he flicks a few drops of water from his wet fingers onto the cream latex wall, the drops beading and running down
K: water drops bead and run down the glossy cream wall, he points at them looking at the camera
text: ¿Cómo sabes si tu pared es mineral? La prueba de la gota. Le tiras unas gotas de agua. Si resbalan como en un vidrio, hay plástico.

A: he flicks water drops onto a bare scraped patch of grey plaster, the drops soaking in and darkening it
K: a dark damp spot on the bare grey plaster where the drops soaked in, he points at it with a satisfied face
text: Si se chupan y la pared se oscurece, es mineral. Ahí la cal se va a agarrar.

A: he scrapes the old latex paint with a wide putty knife, a flake curling off
K: a curl of cream paint hangs from the putty knife, a patch of bare grey plaster exposed, he looks at the camera
text: Si tu pared tiene pintura vieja, hay que sacarla o, por lo menos, sacar todo lo que está flojo, hasta ver el repello.

A: he taps a smooth white gypsum wall on the other side of the room and shakes his head
K: he rests a hand on the smooth white gypsum wall, shaking his head slightly at the camera
text: Y sobre yeso pintado tampoco. Eso no te lo dicen en los videos: te lo digo yo, para que no tires tu dinero.

A: he puts on clear safety goggles and pulls on rubber gloves at the workbench
K: he wears clear safety goggles and orange rubber gloves, holding his gloved hands up to the camera
text: Antes de abrir la bolsa: gafas y guantes. No es exagerar.

A: he points at his goggles with a gloved finger, very serious
K: his gloved index finger touches the side of his goggles, he looks at the camera very serious
text: La cal y el cemento son cáusticos: te queman la piel. Y la cal en los ojos es una urgencia. Si te salta, agua limpia abundante y al médico.

A: he opens the paper bag of hydrated lime and shows the white powder inside
K: he holds the paper bag open toward the camera, fine white powder inside, dust rising a little
text: Esta es cal hidratada, la de construcción. Viene en polvo, en bolsa, en cualquier ferretería.

A: he rubs a pinch of lime between his gloved fingers
K: a little white powder falls from his gloved fingertips, he looks at the camera
text: No es yeso ni es cal viva. La viva es la que hierve con el agua y quema. Esta ya está apagada.

A: he shakes his head and wags a gloved finger at the bag, warning
K: he wags his gloved index finger beside the bag, a warning face at the camera
text: Y cuidado en la ferretería: hay cal agrícola, que es piedra molida para la tierra. Esa no endurece en la pared. Pide cal hidratada, de construcción.

A: he tilts the bag and explains the old tradition with a nostalgic smile
K: he holds the bag against his chest, nostalgic half smile at the camera
text: Así se pintaban las bardas de las escuelas, las casas del campo, las iglesias. Nada nuevo. Lo nuevo es que se olvidó.

A: he puts the bag down and picks up the small bag of white cement, comparing both
K: he holds the small bag of white cement up beside the lime bag, looking at the camera
text: ¿Y para qué el cemento blanco? La cal sola es de adentro. Afuera, donde pega la lluvia, el cemento le da más dureza al frote.

A: he taps the lime bag, then the cement bag, then holds up four fingers and one finger
K: he holds up four fingers on one hand and one on the other, looking at the camera
text: Pero es poquito. Si le pones mucho cemento, queda más dura, pero respira menos y se puede cuartear.

A: he lays out tools on the bench one by one: a wide brush, two buckets, a jug, a piece of green mosquito mesh and a pump sprayer
K: the tools lie in a row on the bench, he points along them with his gloved hand, looking at the camera
text: Las herramientas: una brocha ancha, dos baldes, una jarra, un pedazo de mosquitero y un rociador de jardín, o una botella con atomizador.

A: he picks up the wide brush and flexes its thick bristles against his gloved palm
K: he holds the wide brush up to the camera, bristles fanned out, looking at the camera
text: La brocha, ancha y de cerda gruesa, porque carga mucha cal aguada. El rodillo sirve, pero con brocha la cal entra mejor en los poros.

A: he puts his gloved hand on the lime bag, the small cement bag and the salt jar in turn
K: his gloved hand rests on the salt jar next to the two bags, he looks at the camera with a small smile
text: ¿Y cuánto gastas? Una bolsa de cal, una bolsa chica de cemento blanco y sal gruesa. Cuesta una fracción de una lata de pintura.

A: he scoops lime powder with the jug into a grey bucket, the night before, a lamp on
K: he empties the fourth jug of lime into the bucket, white dust floating, looking into the bucket
text: La noche anterior: cuatro jarras de cal en el balde vacío. Primero el polvo.

d1: close view of water pouring slowly from a jug onto a heap of white lime powder in a bucket, forming a wet crater
d2: the same bucket with the powder soaked into a thick wet white paste, a thin layer of water on top
text: Después el agua, de a poco, y lo dejo que se empape solo.

A: he stirs the thick lime paste with a wooden stick, working hard
K: he leans over the bucket stirring the thick white paste with a wooden stick, focused, sleeves rolled up
text: Revuelvo hasta que no quede polvo seco. Queda una pasta espesa, como crema.

A: he pours a thin layer of water on top of the lime paste and puts the lid on the bucket
K: he presses the lid onto the bucket with both hands, looking at the camera
text: Le dejo un dedo de agua encima, tapo, y a dormir. Mínimo una noche.

A: he taps the lid with his knuckles and explains to the camera
K: his knuckles resting on the bucket lid, he looks at the camera explaining with a calm face
text: ¿Para qué el reposo? Para que la cal se hidrate bien. Si la usas recién mezclada, queda más arenosa y se agarra peor.

d1: close view of a bucket lid being lifted off, revealing a smooth creamy white lime putty under a thin clear layer of water
d2: the lid fully off, the smooth white lime putty surface with a little clear water on top
text: Al día siguiente, mira qué cremosa quedó.

A: he adds water from a large jug into the lime putty and stirs, the mixture turning to milk
K: he stirs a thin milky white liquid in the bucket with the stick, looking at the camera
text: Ahora le agrego agua hasta que quede líquida. Tiene que chorrear del palo, fina, como leche.

A: he lifts the stick out of the bucket and lets the white liquid drip back, showing the camera
K: he holds the stick above the bucket, a thin stream of milky white liquid running off it, looking at the camera
text: ¿Ves cómo chorrea? Si queda pastosa, pintas una capa gruesa, y la capa gruesa es la que se cuartea y se cae.

A: he dissolves coarse salt in a steaming mug of hot water with a spoon
K: he stirs the mug with a spoon, steam rising, the salt nearly gone, looking at the camera
text: Ahora la sal. Un puñado en un poco de agua caliente, y la revuelvo hasta que no quede ni un grano.

d1: close view of a mug of hot water with coarse salt crystals dissolving as a spoon stirs
d2: the same mug with clear water and no crystals left, the spoon resting in it
text: Disuelta. Nunca en grano directo en el balde.

A: he pours the salt water from the mug into the bucket and stirs
K: he stirs the bucket, the empty mug on the bench beside it, looking down at the mix
text: La echo al balde, y revuelvo bien.

A: he mixes one jug of white cement with a little water in a small separate bucket into a thin cream
K: he stirs a small bucket with thin grey-white cement cream, looking at the camera
text: Y el cemento, la jarra de cemento blanco, primero aparte con un poco de agua, para que no haga bolitas.

d1: close view of thin white cement cream being poured from a small bucket into a larger bucket of milky limewash
d2: the milky limewash with a creamy swirl of cement blending into it
text: Y ahora sí, todo junto.

A: he stirs the full bucket slowly for a long time with the stick
K: he keeps stirring the full bucket, looking at the camera with a patient face
text: Revuelvo un buen rato. Y lo voy revolviendo también mientras pinto, porque el cemento se va al fondo.

A: he pours the limewash through green mosquito mesh stretched over another bucket
K: he holds the empty bucket tilted over the mesh, a few lumps left on the green mesh, looking at the camera
text: Y lo último: la cuelo por un pedazo de mosquitero. Lo que queda arriba no va a la pared.

A: he lifts the full bucket onto the bench with both hands, showing how full it is
K: the full bucket of white limewash sits on the bench, he rests his hands on its rim, looking at the camera
text: Con estas medidas me sale casi un balde lleno. Y lo que no uses hoy, ya sabes: con cemento adentro, no se guarda.

A: the neighbor walks into the garage door on the left, looks into the bucket and frowns, talking to the presenter
K: the neighbor stands in the garage doorway leaning to look at the bucket, frowning with a hand on his hip, the presenter beside the bench
line: ¿Y la sal? ¿Vas a pintar o vas a hacer un guiso?
text: ¿Y la sal? ¿Vas a pintar o vas a hacer un guiso?

A: he laughs and points at the salt jar, talking to the neighbor, then to the camera
K: he laughs looking at the camera, pointing at the salt jar on the bench, the neighbor still in the doorway
text: ¡Ja! Eso mismo dicen todos. La sal es el truco de los viejos albañiles. Ya vas a ver, vecino.

A: he puts the bucket down, takes off one glove and picks up a printed sheet of paper from the bench
K: he holds a printed sheet of cream paper in his bare hand, looking at the camera, serious
text: Y ahora presta muchísima atención a esta imagen, porque probablemente sea la parte más importante del video.
Aquí está todo en una sola hoja. Los materiales: cuatro jarras de cal hidratada, una de cemento blanco, un puñado de sal gruesa disuelta, y agua hasta leche.
El paso a paso: la cal remojada desde la noche anterior, colada. La pared limpia, sin pintura plástica, y humedecida.
Tres o cuatro manos finas con brocha ancha, cruzadas, dejando secar entre mano y mano. Y los días siguientes, un rocío de agua para que cure.
Y abajo, los tres errores que la hacen caer: pintar encima de pintura plástica, dar una sola mano gruesa, y pintar con el sol de mediodía pegando en la pared.
Si te quedas con esta hoja, ya puedes pintar. Tómale captura si quieres.

A: he puts the sheet down on the bench and talks casually to the camera
K: he leans on the workbench with one hand on the printed sheet, relaxed, looking at the camera
text: Esto lo tengo ordenado junto con otros arreglos en la guía del canal. Si estás en el televisor, apunta la cámara de tu teléfono a este código.

A: he taps the sheet and nods, relaxed
K: he stands relaxed with his arms folded, a friendly look at the camera
text: Y si estás en el teléfono, el enlace está abajo. Seguimos, que ahora viene la pared.

A: he walks to the old grey half of the exterior wall carrying a bucket and a wire brush
K: he stands in front of the old grey half of the wall with a wire brush in one hand and the bucket at his feet, looking at the camera
text: Esta es la otra mitad de la pared. Repello de cemento, con restos de una pintura vieja que se estaba pelando.

A: he scrapes the peeling old paint with a wide putty knife, flakes falling to the ground
K: he holds the putty knife against the wall, a clean grey scraped area, pale flakes on the ground, looking at the camera
text: Todo lo que se levanta, afuera. Con la espátula, hasta que no salga nada más.

d1: close view of a wide steel putty knife scraping off curling flakes of old off-white paint from grey cement plaster
d2: the same patch now bare grey plaster with scratch marks, a few flakes falling
text: Lo que está bien pegado, lo dejo; lo que suena hueco, lo saco.

A: he scrubs the scraped area with the wire brush, dust flying
K: he brushes the wall with the wire brush, a little grey dust in the air, focused on the wall
text: Después, cepillo de alambre, para sacar el polvo y lo suelto. La cal se pega a la pared, no al polvo.

A: he rubs a damp dark patch at the bottom of the wall with his fingers and shows the camera
K: he crouches by the base of the wall, his fingers on a dark damp stain near the ground, looking up at the camera
text: Y ojo con esto: si la pared tiene humedad que sube del piso, primero hay que resolver eso. La pintura no arregla una humedad.

A: he stands up and brushes his hands, talking to the camera
K: he stands brushing dust off his hands, looking at the camera
text: Donde hay una mancha así, la cal sí deja respirar la pared mejor que un plástico. Pero si el agua sigue subiendo, va a seguir manchando.

A: he spreads an old plastic sheet on the ground along the wall and tapes plastic over a nearby window frame
K: plastic sheeting covers the ground and the window frame, he presses the tape down, looking at the camera
text: Antes de pintar, tapa el piso y las ventanas. La cal salpica, y en los vidrios y en el aluminio deja manchas que cuestan mucho sacar.

A: he wipes a white splash off the window glass with a wet rag
K: he holds the wet rag against the clean glass, looking at the camera
text: Si te cae una gota, límpiala en el momento con un trapo mojado. Fresca sale fácil; seca, ya no tanto.

A: he walks to the end of the wall where a section of bare red brick is exposed and taps it
K: his hand rests on the bare red brick section at the end of the wall, he looks at the camera
text: ¿Y sobre ladrillo sin repellar? También agarra muy bien. El ladrillo chupa más: mójalo más, y cuenta con una mano extra.

A: he pumps the garden sprayer and sprays water on the bare plaster, which darkens
K: he sprays the grey plaster, a large dark wet area, he looks at the camera over his shoulder
text: Ahora la mojo. Esto es lo que casi todos se saltan, y es lo más importante.

d1: close view of a fine spray of water hitting dry grey cement plaster, the surface darkening where it lands
d2: the whole patch evenly dark and damp, tiny droplets on the surface
text: Húmeda, no chorreando.

A: he touches the damp wall with his palm and explains
K: his palm flat on the damp dark wall, he looks at the camera explaining
text: ¿Por qué? Porque una pared seca le chupa el agua a la cal en un segundo. Y la cal, sin agua, no se agarra: queda polvo.

A: he looks up at the sky shading his eyes with his hand, then back to the camera
K: he shades his eyes with his hand looking up at the overcast sky, then looks at the camera
text: Por eso tampoco se pinta con el sol del mediodía pegando de frente. Yo pinto temprano o a la tarde, o con el día nublado como hoy.

A: he checks the weather on his old phone and puts it back in his apron pocket
K: he slides the phone into the apron pocket, looking at the camera with a practical face
text: Y mira el pronóstico: que no llueva en los dos días siguientes, ni que vaya a helar. La cal fresca necesita esos días tranquilos.

A: he stirs the bucket of limewash with the stick and talks to the camera, thoughtful
K: he holds the stick still in the bucket, looking at the camera with a thoughtful face
text: Te cuento algo. Me escribió Ramiro, de Cochabamba, en Bolivia. Pintó la barda de su patio con cal y cemento.

A: he rubs his hand on the old grey wall and shows his palm to the camera, imitating the story
K: he shows his palm to the camera with a little grey dust on it, eyebrows raised
text: A los pocos meses pasaba la mano por la pared y le quedaba blanca. Y me dijo: esto no sirve.

A: he raises one finger, then two, then three while talking
K: he holds up three fingers, looking at the camera with a knowing face
text: Le pregunté tres cosas. ¿La mojaste antes? No. ¿A qué hora pintaste? Al mediodía. ¿Cuántas manos? Una, bien gruesa, para terminar rápido.

A: he nods slowly, half smiling, then points at the wall
K: he points at the grey wall with the stick, a patient half smile at the camera
text: Las tres cosas que la hacen fallar, juntas. No era la receta: era cómo la puso.

A: he dips the wide brush into the bucket and wipes the excess on the rim
K: he holds the loaded brush above the bucket, wiping it on the rim, looking at the camera
text: Así que vamos a hacerlo bien. Brocha ancha, cargada pero sin chorrear.

A: he paints the damp grey wall with wide crossing strokes
K: he paints a wide area with crossing strokes, the fresh coat translucent milky over the grey, his face turned to the wall
text: Pinceladas cruzadas, en todas direcciones, y metiendo la cal en los poros.

A: he reaches up and paints a full band along the top of the wall from one corner, moving sideways
K: a fresh band of translucent white runs along the top of the wall, he paints near the corner, face turned to the wall
text: Y un orden: de arriba hacia abajo, y un paño completo de esquina a esquina, sin parar a la mitad. Si paras a la mitad, se nota la marca.

d1: close view of a wide brush pushing thin limewash into the pores of rough grey plaster with crossing strokes
d2: the same area covered in a thin translucent milky white layer, the brush lifting
text: Se aprieta un poquito, para que entre.

A: he steps back and looks at the translucent first coat, showing it to the camera with a hand
K: he stands a step back, his open hand toward the translucent patchy coat on the wall, looking at the camera
text: Y aquí es donde la gente se asusta. Mira: se ve transparente, manchada. Parece que no sirve.

A: the neighbor looks over the low brick wall at the translucent patchy wall and laughs, talking to the presenter
K: the neighbor leans his forearms on the low brick wall, laughing, pointing at the patchy wall with his chin, the presenter standing with the brush
line: ¿Y eso es pintura? Se ve más gris que antes, hombre.
text: ¿Y eso es pintura? Se ve más gris que antes, hombre.

A: he smiles at the neighbor and taps the side of his nose, then talks to the camera
K: he looks at the camera with a calm confident smile, the brush in his hand, the neighbor behind the low wall
text: Espérate a que seque. La cal mojada se ve gris y transparente. Al secarse se pone blanca, blanca tiza.

d1: close view of a wet translucent greyish limewash patch on a wall drying and turning bright white
d2: the same patch now dry and bright chalky white
text: Así.

A: he checks his watch and holds up his hand with fingers spread
K: he shows the camera his wristwatch, his other hand with five fingers spread, looking at the camera
text: Entre mano y mano, de cuatro a seis horas, según el calor. Que esté seca al tacto, pero que no pase un día entero.

A: he sprays the dried first coat lightly with the pump sprayer before the second coat
K: a light mist on the first coat, he lowers the sprayer and looks at the camera
text: Y antes de la segunda mano, un rocío otra vez. Siempre sobre húmedo.

A: he paints the second coat with long crossing strokes, the wall turning whiter
K: the wall is noticeably whiter, still a little uneven, he paints with the wide brush, focused
text: Segunda mano. Ahora sí empieza a tapar. Todavía se ven sombras, y está bien.

A: he stirs the bucket again with the stick before loading the brush
K: he stirs the bucket, the brush resting across the rim, looking at the camera
text: Cada tanto revuelvo el balde. Si no, el cemento se va al fondo y la última mano sale aguada.

A: he paints the third coat on the wall, the white becoming even
K: the wall is evenly white and matte, he finishes a stroke at the top with the brush, looking at the result
text: Tercera mano. Esta es la que la deja pareja.

d1: close view of a wide brush laying a final coat of limewash on an already white wall, the surface becoming smooth and even
d2: the wall surface evenly bright chalky white and matte, the brush gone from the frame
text: Si todavía ves transparencias, una cuarta. Nunca una gruesa: varias finitas.

A: he steps back and runs his hand in the air over the finish, talking about the look
K: he stands back with his open hand toward the finished matte white wall, looking at the camera
text: El acabado es mate, tipo tiza. No brilla como la pintura de lata. Si buscas brillo, esto no es para ti.

A: he points at a thin hairline crack in the white wall near the window
K: his fingertip rests beside a thin hairline crack in the white wall, he looks at the camera
text: Si la pared tiene grietas finas, la cal las rellena un poco. Pero una grieta que se mueve vuelve a aparecer. Esa se arregla antes de pintar.

A: he shows a small cup of red iron oxide pigment powder to the camera
K: he holds a small plastic cup of reddish earth pigment powder toward the camera
text: ¿Y con color? Sí, pero con pigmentos minerales, los óxidos en polvo, los que se usan para el cemento.

d1: close view of red iron oxide pigment powder being stirred into a small bucket of white limewash, turning it pale terracotta
d2: the small bucket with an even pale terracotta pink liquid, the stick resting on the rim
text: Primero en un poco de agua, y después al balde. Salen tonos suaves: arena, rosado, ocre, gris.

A: he paints a small test stroke of the pale terracotta color on a scrap of plaster board
K: he holds the scrap board up to the camera with a pale terracotta test stroke on it
text: Y prueba siempre en un pedazo antes. Seco, queda mucho más claro que mojado.

A: he puts the scrap board down and talks to the camera, remembering the story
K: he leans the scrap board against the wall and looks at the camera with a warm smile
text: Ah, y Ramiro. Volvió a pintar su barda así: mojada, temprano, en manos finas. Me mandó foto del antes y el después.

A: he rubs the white wall and shows the clean palm, smiling
K: he holds his clean palm up to the camera, smiling, the white wall behind him
text: Y esta vez, la mano limpia. Dijo que ya no le mancha la ropa a los niños cuando se recargan.

A: he wipes his hands on a rag and talks casually to the camera
K: he holds the rag, relaxed, looking at the camera
text: Por cosas como esa armé la guía del canal: los arreglos con sus medidas y sus errores, para no depender de nadie.

A: he gestures down toward the bottom of the frame with his hand
K: he points down toward the bottom of the frame with his hand, friendly look at the camera
text: Si estás en el televisor, el código está en pantalla. Si estás en el teléfono, el enlace está abajo, en la descripción.

A: he mists the finished white wall with the pump sprayer, a fine mist floating
K: a fine mist floats in front of the white wall, he holds the sprayer, looking at the camera
text: Terminaste de pintar. Pero la cal no terminó. Ahora empieza a endurecer, y tarda.

A: he taps the wall with his knuckles and explains, calm
K: his knuckles rest on the white wall, he looks at the camera explaining
text: La cal se endurece tomando el aire. Es lento: semanas. Y para que lo haga bien, necesita un poco de humedad.

A: he holds up three fingers and then sprays once more
K: he holds up three fingers with the sprayer in the other hand, looking at the camera
text: Por eso, los dos o tres días siguientes, un rocío de agua a la mañana y otro a la tarde. Rocío, no manguera.

A: he points to a piece of old cloth hanging to shade the wall
K: he points at an old sheet hung from the eaves shading part of the wall, looking at the camera
text: Y si le va a pegar sol fuerte o viento, la tapo con una tela. Que no se seque de golpe.

A: he washes the wide brush in a bucket of clean water, the water turning milky
K: he lifts the clean brush out of the milky water, looking at the camera
text: Cuando termines, lava la brocha y los baldes con agua, enseguida. Y lo que sobra con cemento no lo tires por la cañería: se endurece adentro.

A: he pats the wall and puts the sprayer down, satisfied
K: he puts the sprayer down at his feet, standing beside the white wall, satisfied look at the camera
text: Y ahora, lo que te prometí al principio. Pero antes, te muestro la versión de adentro.

A: he walks into a small bedroom with a bare grey plastered wall and puts a bucket down
K: he stands in front of the bare grey plastered bedroom wall with the bucket at his feet, looking at the camera
text: Para adentro, en un cuarto, yo no le pongo cemento. Uso la receta de la guía: cal sola, sal y agua.

A: he pours milky limewash from a jug into a small bucket
K: he holds the jug above the small bucket, a thin stream of milky liquid, looking at the camera
text: Una jarra de cal por dos o tres de agua, hasta leche fina. La misma idea, sin el cemento.

A: he paints the bare interior wall with wide crossing strokes
K: he paints the grey wall with wide crossing strokes, a translucent milky coat, his face turned to the wall
text: Adentro no la lava la lluvia, y la cal sola respira mejor. Es muy buena en cuartos donde se junta humedad.

A: he opens the bedroom window wide, then turns back to the camera
K: he stands by the wide open window, one hand on the frame, looking at the camera
text: Adentro, pinta con la ventana abierta, y ten a los niños y a las mascotas lejos del balde mientras trabajas.

A: he points at a corner of the ceiling with a small dark mould stain
K: he points up at a dark mould stain in the corner of the ceiling, looking at the camera
text: Además, la cal es alcalina. Al moho no le gusta nada. Por eso se usaba en cocinas, baños y establos.

A: he touches the painted wall with a finger and shows it, honest face
K: he holds up his fingertip toward the camera, a trace of white on it, an honest face
text: Ahora, los límites, porque no todo es perfecto. Recién pintada, si la frotas, puede soltar un poquito de polvo.

A: he rubs a dry older section of the wall and shows a clean finger
K: he holds up a clean fingertip toward the camera, the old painted section behind him
text: Cuando cura bien, eso casi desaparece. Pero una cal mal hecha, sin mojar la pared, con los años suelta polvo al frotarla.

A: he shakes his head and wags his finger lightly
K: he wags his index finger lightly, a small smile at the camera
text: Y no es pintura lavable. Una mancha de grasa no se va con trapo y jabón: se retoca con otra mano de cal, que para eso es barata.

A: he picks up the bucket and walks toward the door
K: he stands at the doorway of the bedroom with the bucket in his hand, looking back at the camera
text: Y cuesta una fracción de una lata de pintura. Por eso, si se ensucia, no duele volver a pasarle.

A: he stops at the door and raises a finger, remembering
K: he stands at the doorway with his index finger raised, eyebrows up, looking at the camera
text: Ah, una cosa. Hay una variante de esto que funciona todavía mejor en paredes que se mojan mucho con la lluvia.

A: he points down toward the bottom of the frame with a knowing smile
K: he points down toward the bottom of the frame, a knowing smile at the camera
text: Te dejé exactamente cómo hacerla en la descripción.

A: he walks out to the exterior wall, now fully white, and picks up the green garden hose
K: he stands in front of the fully white wall holding the green hose pistol, looking at the camera with a small smile
text: Pasaron varios días. La pared completa, las dos mitades, curadas.

A: he presses a strip of masking tape firmly on the dry white wall and pulls it off, showing it to the camera
K: he holds up the strip of tape toward the camera, the tape almost clean with only a faint white trace, the white wall behind him
text: Primero, la cinta, la misma prueba que hice adentro. La aprieto, la arranco... y casi limpia.

A: the neighbor comes up to the low brick wall with a coffee mug, looks at the white wall and talks to the presenter, sceptical
K: the neighbor rests his mug on the low brick wall, eyebrows raised, pointing at the hose with his free hand
line: A ver, genio. Dale con la manguera, que yo quiero ver.
text: A ver, genio. Dale con la manguera, que yo quiero ver.

A: he sprays the white wall hard with the hose, water running down
K: he sprays the white wall at close range, water streaming down, the paint intact, he looks at the neighbor
text: Con gusto.

d1: close view of a strong jet of water hitting a chalky white limewashed wall, water running in streams down the surface
d2: the same wet white wall with water still running, the white paint intact, a few drops falling from the edge

A: he turns off the hose and rubs the wet wall with his palm, then shows the palm
K: he holds his wet palm up toward the neighbor and the camera, the palm clean, water dripping from the wall
text: Froto la pared mojada, y nada. Ni se ablanda ni se va.

A: he lifts the hose pistol and shows the nozzle to the camera, explaining
K: he holds the dripping hose pistol up beside his face, looking at the camera, eyebrows raised
text: Y esto es con el chorro a presión, de cerca. La lluvia le pega mucho más suave que esto.

A: the neighbor leans closer, rubs the wall with his own finger, looks at his clean finger and shrugs, talking to the presenter
K: the neighbor looks at his clean fingertip with a grudging face, shrugging, the presenter smiling beside the wall
line: Bueno... me callo. Pero la receta me la pasas, ¿eh?
text: Bueno... me callo. Pero la receta me la pasas, ¿eh?

A: he laughs and gives a thumbs up to the neighbor, then turns to the camera
K: he looks at the camera laughing, thumb still up, the neighbor behind the low wall
text: Te la paso, vecino. Y ahora sí, lo que te prometí: el error del cuarto ingrediente.

A: he holds up the glass jar of coarse salt to the camera, serious
K: he holds the jar of coarse salt at face height, a serious face at the camera
text: La sal ayuda a que la cal seque más despacio y agarre mejor. Pero es un puñado por balde. Uno. No más.

A: he points at a white powdery bloom stain on an old wall in the corner of the patio
K: he points at a white fluffy salt stain on an old wall near the ground, looking at the camera
text: Si te pasas de sal, la pared te la devuelve: salen estas manchas blancas, como pelusa, y la cal se suelta ahí.

A: he shakes the salt jar and then puts it down on the low wall
K: the salt jar sits on the low brick wall, he looks at the camera with his arms crossed, calm
text: Y siempre disuelta en agua caliente. En grano se queda en puntitos, y cada puntito es un lugar donde se va a soltar.

A: he holds the pump sprayer and talks to the camera, calm
K: he holds the pump sprayer lowered, looking at the camera, calm
text: Poca sal, bien disuelta, y la pared húmeda durante el curado.

A: he mists the white wall with the sprayer one more time
K: a light mist floats in front of the white wall, he looks at the camera with a small nod
text: Eso es lo que casi nadie hace bien. Y es lo que hace que no se caiga.

A: he stands at the line where the old wall used to be, gesturing to the whole white wall
K: he stands in front of the fully white wall with his arms open, looking at the camera
text: Así que, ¿loco o genio? Ninguno de los dos. Esto es lo que hacían los abuelos, y lo olvidamos porque la lata es más cómoda.

A: he counts on his fingers the key rules while talking
K: he holds up four fingers, looking at the camera, serious and friendly
text: Cuatro de cal, una de cemento, un puñado de sal disuelta, agua hasta leche. Pared mineral y mojada. Manos finas. Curado con rocío.

A: he picks up the bucket and brush and points at the camera
K: he holds the bucket and brush, pointing the brush toward the camera with a smile
text: Si lo haces así, tienes una pared que respira, que no se descascara, y que cuesta muy poco.

A: he gestures toward the back corner of the house, suggesting a small test
K: he points toward the back corner of the house with his brush, a friendly look at the camera
text: Y si te da miedo, pruébala primero en un pedazo chico, atrás de la casa. Una semana. Si te convence, pintas todo.

A: he puts the bucket down and talks to the camera, relaxed
K: he stands relaxed with one hand on his apron, looking at the camera
text: La hoja con todo, y los demás arreglos de la casa, están en la guía del canal. El código en pantalla o el enlace abajo.

A: he nods to the neighbor behind the low wall and back to the camera, warm
K: he waves goodbye at the camera with a warm smile, the neighbor behind the low wall raising his mug
text: Y cuéntame en los comentarios qué pared vas a pintar. Nos vemos en el próximo arreglo.
